term: per accidens (accidentally) ordered series of causes
definition: A multiplication of causes in which a cause acts in its own right and its having been caused by a predecessor is accidental to its present causing: a craftsman successively uses different hammers, or a man generates as man rather than as son of his father. The source reading that an infinite series of this kind is not impossible is retained in STMT-INFINITE-REGRESS-IMPOSSIBLE-ONLY-IN-PER-SE-SERIES. Its current two-Prop Lean declaration is an opaque transcription, not a model of history or a proof of metaphysical possibility. Analyst sibling STMT-PER-SE-HISTORICAL-SERIES-DISTINCTION types a more limited claim: a distinct historical-predecessor relation can have an injective infinite chain while essential dependence on the same members is well-founded and nonempty. No first historical member is assumed. This witnesses formal compatibility only, not that all per-accidens series are possible, that an actual infinite past exists, or that the relations satisfy the source intended causal meaning.
note: The relation-level witness and explicit dictionary contrast are recorded in docs/causal-regress-and-grim-reapers.md. Interpreting the primitive historical relation as time, and independence of present power from the removal of historical predecessors, remain OPEN bridges. Arbitrarily long finite chains and one infinite Nat-indexed chain are distinct claims. Root routes retain their essential no-regress assumptions. Sense-index investigation (2026-11-09): no existing declaration faithfully supplies SERIES_OF_CAUSES_2. HistoricalLinksAreEssential is an inclusion dictionary, not a historical-series type; DescendingPerSeSeries H f constrains only adjacent edges and does not encode time or survival of present causing; EssentialDependenceCompatibleWithHistoricalDescent is one existential compatibility proposition, not the definition of each accidental series. None is a faithful replacement binding. A completed interpretation needs an explicit clock/precedence input and a present-power response under removal of a historical predecessor, with the independence condition tested on that response. The meaning of removal must distinguish preventing original generation from removing the predecessor after generation. Whether independence means every admissible post-generation removal or a selected intervention remains an owner semantic choice. No new attribution or premise discharge is made. The owner authorized an analyst sibling using a selected post-generation removal response (Historical selected-removal configuration); it is deliberately narrower than the sourced reading and is not identified with SERIES_OF_CAUSES_2. Universal admissible-removal independence remains unencoded.
